text:
Recent work supports intent-preserving self-supervision, while warning that sequence augmentation can distort preferences. ICSRec (WSDM 2024) jointly trains next-item prediction with cross-subsequence intent objectives and masks likely false negatives: different subsequences can express the same intent and should not automatically repel each other. ICMA (COLING 2025) combines temporal information, item-relevance augmentation and sequence–intent consistency. These motivate auxiliary objectives, but do not establish that adjacent interactions always share intent. [ICSRec](https://doi.org/10.1145/3616855.3635773), [ICMA](https://aclanthology.org/2025.coling-main.222/).

Temporal information offers another signal: TemProxRec (2024) contrasts items selected in nearby time periods across users and models within-history time gaps. EICD-Rec (2025) explicitly addresses augmentation-amplified noise and same-intent false negatives; its category-based explicit-intent component requires metadata unavailable here. IeSRec (2026) further explores intent-preserving subsequence augmentation and jointly optimized intent losses. These findings favor cautious view construction over unrestricted cropping, masking or reordering. [TemProxRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.09784), [EICD-Rec](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-025-03047-y), [IeSRec](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44443-026-01197-1).

A compatible experimental hypothesis: retain one shared GRU predictor per category and add a small consistency loss between order-preserving, overlapping history views ending at the same interaction. Use training histories only; avoid enforcing agreement across suspected intent changes, and mask duplicate-target pairs if using in-batch negatives. Compare against the corrected GRU baseline and gate-only variant under identical budgets. This adaptation is an inference from the literature; persistent-preference separation and recent-intent gains remain unproven until execution checks pass and official macro validation HR@10 improves.
